title: Customer Churn Analysis Report
executive_summary: This report analyzes a snapshot of 749 customers to identify churn drivers. The overall churn rate is 37.7%. Key findings indicate that contract type is the strongest predictor of churn, with monthly contracts associated with significantly higher attrition. An at-risk segment of 100 customers with high support tickets and low satisfaction shows a critical churn rate of 71.0%. Lifetime value scales substantially with plan tier.

key_findings.statement: The dataset contains 749 customers with an overall churn rate of 37.7% and an average monthly fee of $42.1.
Churn rates are relatively stable across plans, ranging from 36.6% (Premium) to 38.9% (Basic). The Basic plan has the highest churn rate.
Churn rates by signup cohort show minor variation, with the 2024 cohort having the highest rate at 39.8%.
Contract type has a major impact on retention. Monthly contracts have a 48.3% churn rate compared to 21.9% for annual contracts, representing a 121.1% increase.
An at-risk segment of 100 customers with high support tickets and low satisfaction exhibits a churn rate of 71.0%.
Customer tenure averages 20.8 months with a standard deviation of 13.2 months. The average satisfaction score is 3.4, with 27 customers missing a score.
Lifetime value increases significantly with plan tier. Premium customers have an average LTV of $1,817, which is 292.0% higher than the Basic plan LTV of $463.

limitations: The analysis is based on a single snapshot and does not track individual customer behavior over time.
Satisfaction scores are missing for 27 customers, potentially biasing the satisfaction mean.
Causality cannot be inferred; observed associations (e.g., contract type and churn) may be influenced by unobserved factors.
conclusion: To reduce churn, the business should prioritize converting monthly customers to annual contracts and intervene with the high-risk segment showing low satisfaction. While plan tier has a minor effect on churn rates, it significantly impacts lifetime value, suggesting retention efforts across all plans remain valuable.
